key_facts: BBC Panorama, in a joint investigation with the Bureau of Investigative Journalism, reports that Deloitte Cyprus signed off accounts for Abramovich's Cypriot company Amiscan Investments in which assets worth $672m (£508m), including superyachts, mansions and private jets, disappeared from the company's accounts.

According to the leaked documents, the assets were transferred to a British Virgin Islands parent company and the change was backdated by three years to 2003 to circumvent a 2006 Cypriot transparency law; Deloitte Cyprus reviewed the backdated documents and deemed them "adequate", and signed the 2003 accounts in 2006, leaving only $75,000 of assets.

Panorama also reports evidence of a tax evasion scheme involving Kravin Investments, which held almost $2bn in a bank in 2003 and earned large interest, with Abramovich's advisers allegedly using backdated documents to avoid tax in Cyprus.

Abramovich's lawyers deny that he evaded tax or concealed his fortune, say Panorama provided no evidence he knew about or directed the falsification, and state it is legitimate to rely on professional advice; Deloitte Cyprus says it "acts in compliance with applicable laws".
importance_reason: Расследование о возможном участии Big Four-аудитора в подделке документов и уклонении от налогов связано с крупным активом под санкциями; фактический охват ограничен, а значимость зависит от дальнейших юридических последствий.

key_facts: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said AI is hitting the global labor market like a "slow-moving tsunami", with young graduates most exposed; she estimated about 40% of jobs worldwide will eventually be "augmented, downgraded or eliminated" (about 60% exposure in advanced economies, 23% in low-income countries).

Tharman Shanmugaratnam, co-chair of the World Bank Jobs Council, called for "crisis-era" employment support measures (used during Covid-19 and the global financial crisis) to become a permanent part of structural policy, including incentives for firms to hire fresh graduates; he said demand for graduates in the U.S. has fallen "for the first time in a century".

World Bank President Ajay Banga estimated 1.2 billion young people will turn 18 over the next 15 years, and that the private sector, which generates 75% to 85% of jobs in any country, will have to absorb most of them.

Georgieva said AI adoption could lift growth by 0.5–1 percentage point in advanced Asia and 0.2–0.8 percentage point in emerging Asia; AI-related investment and trade have helped keep global expansion near 3% despite an energy supply shock.
importance_reason: Аналитический обзор позиций МВФ и Всемирного банка без решения регулятора или рыночного события; значим как тренд политики, но без прямого немедленного рыночного эффекта.

key_facts: About 1.5 million people in the UK are not on the mains gas network and rely on heating oil, mostly in rural locations; the heating oil market is unregulated, so global price changes pass quickly to customers.

According to Boiler Juice, the heating oil price was about 60p per litre until March 2026, rose to a high of 134ppl after the war in Iran began in March, dipped in recent months and currently stands at 111ppl.

The CMA said heating oil customers in remote areas are too vulnerable to price shocks and called for stronger safeguards, including regulatory oversight; Action in Rural Communities England asks the government to remove VAT on heating oil and LPG for six months.

The Department for the Environment and Net Zero says it is helping households switch from heating oil to clean heat with grants worth £9,000 and a resilience fund for areas with higher rates of oil heating; the source does not give the statement's full scope.
